checkpoints: A burst of multiple edits saves exactly once, 120 ms after the last edit, using the latest text.
A later edit burst schedules and completes another save.
An empty-string edit is saved rather than mistaken for no pending value.
Edits made with no current view remain a no-op.
Switching documents, reopening the same document, closing, disposing, and Vue unmounting do not lose an accepted pending edit; the edit remains associated with its original document.
A synchronous navigation triggered by a store listener is not overwritten by the older open, close, or retirement operation when that operation resumes.
Status rendering remains filtered to the currently opened document, and retired subscriptions stop receiving status.
Search preview retains its 40 ms trailing behavior and hide cancellation.
Public JavaScript and Vue syntax/build checks pass; these checks do not establish business correctness.
forbidden_effects: Do not continue writing to the store on every editor keystroke.
Do not associate a delayed edit with whichever document happens to be current when the timer fires.
Do not discard an accepted pending edit merely because its view badge or subscription is retired.
Do not allow reentrant flushing to consume the same pending value twice or erase a new burst created during the save callback.
Do not let an outer navigation operation overwrite a newer synchronous navigation initiated by a store listener.
Do not change store event fields, source document identities, text semantics, status filtering, subscription semantics, workspace method signatures, or Vue unmount disposal.
Do not modify the adjacent search preview's 40 ms interval or hide-cancellation behavior.
lifecycle_identity: The pending edit belongs to the document buffer selected when edit(text) is accepted, not to a later current view.
BufferBank entries are keyed by document id and persist independently of the current view badge.
The current view owns the live store subscription; retiring the view removes that subscription without destroying its store-owned document buffer.
Each open request must retain its own authority token so callback-driven navigation can supersede it.

obligations.text: Replace per-keystroke editor writes with the existing trailing-task mechanism: reset the 120 ms timer on each edit in a burst and, after 120 ms of quiet, write only the latest text.
After one burst is consumed, later bursts must be independently schedulable and save successfully, including a latest value of the empty string.
At edit acceptance, use the current view's persistent per-document buffer so delayed saving retains the original document identity; editing without a current view remains a no-op.

Preserve accepted edits across open, close, dispose, and component unmount. Because the original editor made text synchronously available in the store, departure handling must not weaken that observable persistence or allow a destination read to observe pre-edit text.

Before invoking callback-capable store.write during timer or departure flushing, retire the consumed pending timer/value state. Reentrant flushes must not duplicate the value, and edits accepted during the callback must form a later burst.

When departing a view, revoke current-view ownership, detach its captured subscription, and complete its clearing effect before a pending save can synchronously navigate. Any outer open operation must revalidate its request before installing a destination view or rendering its document.

Preserve createWorkspace's open(id), edit(text), close(), and dispose() interfaces; store read/write/subscribe semantics and status payloads; current-document status filtering; and Vue unmount disposal.
Leave createSearchPreview behavior unchanged, including its separate 40 ms quiet interval and hide cancellation.

ordering_barriers: For each push, cancel the preceding timer before scheduling the replacement 120 ms timer.
On flush, snapshot the latest pending value and clear/cancel pending state before calling store.write, since store listeners execute synchronously and may navigate.
On view departure, capture the departing view, clear current ownership, detach its subscription, and render the cleared document state before flushing its pending buffer.

After any departure flush that can synchronously navigate, compare the outer open request with the current request before subscribing, installing a view, reading, or rendering the requested destination.
preservation: Store writes still update the record before synchronously notifying subscribed listeners and retain {id, text, revision} event semantics.
Status events remain rendered only when event.id equals the opened document id.
Per-document buffers remain store-owned and reusable across view lifetimes; view retirement removes only the live subscription.
Document ids and text are unchanged through scheduling and saving.
close(), dispose(), and Vue onBeforeUnmount cleanup remain effective.
Search preview remains transient, uses a distinct 40 ms trailing task, and cancels pending preview work on hide.
scope: Business behavior in src/coordinator.js necessary to route editor edits through persistent per-document trailing buffers and preserve navigation/cleanup behavior.
Existing generic trailing behavior in src/services.js as used by the editor; change it only if required to meet editor burst and reentrancy obligations without changing preview behavior.
Existing Vue teardown integration in src/Workspace.vue is preserved, not redesigned.
No test, configuration, dependency, evaluator, scorer, hidden-test, or reference-implementation changes are authorized.

Laboratory operations — A workspace document buffer persists independently of the current view badge. Save callbacks can synchronously navigate. Preview is transient and owns a different quiet interval. Document-buffer responsibility: store-owned BufferBank

createWorkspace offers open(id), edit(text), close(), dispose(); createSearchPreview offers query(text), hide(). Store read/write/subscribe is synchronous; timer schedule(callback,delay), cancel(handle) is explicitly controlled.

Document buffers are owned by the store BufferBank, while Badge owns only a live subscription. A store listener may call navigation synchronously. All source identities/text and status payloads retain original semantics.
const flush = () => { const saved = value; retire(); if (saved !== null) consume(saved); };
push(text) { if (ticket !== null) timers.cancel(ticket); value = text; ticket = timers.schedule(flush, wait); }

const task = trailing(timers, 40, query => publish({query}));
  return {query: text => task.push(text), hide: () => task.cancel()};

triggers: Calling edit(text) while a document view is current.
Expiration of the editor buffer's 120 ms quiet interval.
A new edit arriving before the current 120 ms timer expires.
Opening another document or reopening the same document while an edit is pending.
Calling close(), dispose(), or Vue component unmount while an edit is pending.
A synchronous store listener navigating during a timer-driven or departure-driven save.
